zach: kicked off a small apples-to-apples replay vs synthetic run to stress streaming vs polling readloops. quick TL;DR: streaming gives lower p50 but p99 regresses at high concurrency when kernels switch and KV hitrate drops. logs attached. anyone else see kernel-induced kv churn?
maya: what load shape? short bursts or steady QPS?
azex: (typo) alex: steady-ish bursts: 200 rps nominal, 800rps spikes for 30s every 2m. seq len ~512, avg generation 120 tokens, chunk size 64 for streaming. polling test used 120 token non-stream single response.
priya: that spike pattern will amplify KV eviction. streaming keeps more concurrent KV windows open, so kernel selection + allocator pressure can evict prefixes. did you record KV hitrates?
zach: yes — attached extract: streaming kv_hitrate ~78% baseline then falls to 52% during spike; polling stayed ~85%. p99 latency jumped 2.3x for streaming during those windows.
maya: hmm. batching heuristics also matter — continuous batching for streaming sometimes groups heterogeneous lengths, causing kernel fallback to slower path. did the run force kernel pinning?
azex: alex: we didn't pin; we let kernel selector adapt. we captured profile: kernel_switch_count spikes correlated with kv_hitrate drops.
priya: can you paste the run command and conf?
azex: alex: sure:
```
./replay-harness --model llama-2-13b-q4 --mode streaming --chunk-size 64 --concurrency 64 --batching=continuous --kv-ttl=10s --enable-kernel-adapt=true
./replay-harness --mode polling --chunk-size 0 --concurrency 64 --batching=fixed --kv-ttl=10s
```
ops-bot: job replay/472 finished: artifacts -> gs://redwood-perf/replays/472.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
priya: two quick experiments to try: 1) increase kv-ttl to 60s, 2) disable dynamic kernel adapt (force best-known kernel) and rerun spikes. that should isolate eviction vs kernel perf.
zach: yup. also want to instrument readloop queue lengths on the client side — suspect streaming readloop lets in-flight items pile up if backpressure not exercised. can we add a client-side cap?
maya: add client param `max_inflight_chunks=8` in the harness and rerun. also try `batching=length_bucket` to keep homogeneous batches.
azex: alex: ok i'll run 3 variants: (A) kv-ttl=60s, (B) kernel_pin, (C) max_inflight_chunks=8 + length_bucket. scheduling them now. will post perf summary in this thread. :thumbsup:
priya: great. if p99 still bad then next step is to capture a kernel profile (nvprof + perf) during the spike and check memcpy/kernel-launch times.
zach: thanks team. keeping this thread focused on methodology so ops/playbook is clear. goal: reproduce cleanly and produce minimal config diffs for perf team to triage. :thinking:
